title: Problem 03
markdown:
### Problem
Determine how many rational numbers there are between 0 and 1 having the property that when written as a fraction in lowest terms, the product of the numerator and the denominator is $17!$.

### Solution (adapted from the official solution)
There are 64 such fractions.

Let the fraction in lowest terms be $p/q$, with $0 < p < q$ and $\gcd(p, q) = 1$. We are given $pq = 17!$.

The prime factors of $17!$ are the primes less than or equal to 17:

$$\{2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13, 17\}.$$

There are 7 distinct prime numbers dividing $17!$.

Since $\gcd(p, q) = 1$, no prime can divide both $p$ and $q$. Therefore, for each of the 7 prime factors $p_k$, the full prime power $p_k^{e_k}$ appearing in the prime factorization of $17!$ must be assigned entirely to either $p$ or $q$.

There are $2^7 = 128$ ways to partition these 7 prime powers between $p$ and $q$.

Because $17!$ is not a perfect square, $p \ne q$ in all cases. In exactly half of these pairs we have $p < q$ (and in the other half $p > q$).

Thus the number of fractions strictly between 0 and 1 is:

$$\frac{2^7}{2} = 2^6 = 64.$$

### Conceptual Explanation
Coprimality forces each distinct prime power of $17!$ to belong entirely to either the numerator or denominator. With 7 distinct primes up to 17, there are $2^7$ subsets. Symmetry $p < q$ divides this count by 2, yielding $2^6 = 64$.

### Key Technique
Partitioning full prime-power components to ensure coprimality and applying order symmetry.
